title: Smart Trading Platform
author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
selftext:
# Problem:

I am currently using 4 different tools and I am sure this the case with lot of people. Those are **charts**, broker dashboard for **execution**, **claude** for analysis and lastly if you are in Algo then **VS code** or colab in another tab.

# Idea:

I am engineer my self and as I though before sometime this should be doable with one single platform containing all 4 things and advanced risk management system (**RMS**) and integrated python SDK. I started building and got one by one issues realizing why no body has made it till now!

Eg: you get web socket feed and to distribute that with chart, scripts, watchlist, live orders you need to manage that stream and fan out that data so perfectly that its not a vibe coding thing you can achieve in a day! This is one of them there are several and lot of them!

# Solution:

Give it a time to build, build underlying architecture by my your self and get partner also to work on this idea.

After almost a year we are almost ready to launch the product in next with 4 different brokers integrated covering us and Indian market

# Product:

We have build a programmable trading platform called [while25](https://while25.com)

It has advanced **charts**, **risk management system**, **order routing** with order engine taking merely taking <1ms from tick to order API, and all other professional trading panels like **options chain**, **multi leg builder**, **future trading**, **DOM**, etc...

**Cherry on the top:** we have made it completely agent friendly and it also has inbuilt **AI assistant** which can look at your cutest positions, charts, analysis, news and code (yes **code editor** is also inbuilt with while25 **python SDK**) so it can watch and modify things and execute whole workflow on users behalf! But it can not touch live money path like placing order or deploying strategy by design.

**Code editor**: This one is really special as it allows trader to go from idea to execution in seconds without worrying about underlying data plumbing, order routing and risk management.

You can build custom indicator and plot it on chart, you can make strategy out of it, you can make custom panel like predicting apple close with ml model and make a dashboard of that, etc

Its python with data and trading api unified for all broker, all asset class and all market!

Let me know if you would be interested to try this out!

Check our more at [while25.com](https://while25.com)

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
How does while25 separate AI edits in the built-in Python SDK editor from code an already-running strategy uses? Preventing the assistant from placing orders or deploying strategies is useful, but edits to a shared module or configuration could still affect live behavior if the running process picks them up.

A useful demo would have the assistant change a sizing function while a strategy is running. Show that the live strategy keeps its approved version until the user explicitly deploys the change, and that the RMS still checks the resulting orders. Does deployment pin both code and configuration?

replies.author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
replies.body:
Worth flagging this one.

So the design is, if any script is mounted AI can not edit it (hard rule). You need to stop it and then only you can edit. Because even if you maintain two separate file buffers you might get caught in some race conditions between reloading or deploying while you/AI just making some changes.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the fan-out point is the real one. one feed into charts, scripts, watchlist and live orders sounds like a plain pub/sub problem until a slow consumer starts backing up the order path, and then the chart is a second behind the fill. did you give the order engine its own socket, or share one and prioritise?

replies.author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
replies.body:
Write are seperate from read operations. Multiple readers can read the live buffer but oy one writer can write to it. So no slow consumer can stall the feed. If your strategy demand tick by tick processing it will have it and charts will still run at 1s cadence if configured that way.

Its part of low level design which is used in domain like OS or Embedded Systems for high throughput low latency system!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: single writer, many readers off a ring is the right shape. the thing I'd still watch is the order path being just another reader. it can read at tick cadence while the chart reads at 1s, fine, but the write side has to never wait on anyone, disk included, or the fill lags exactly when it matters.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: good. then the only thing left to measure is fill timestamp minus tick timestamp on a busy open, p99 not median. that number tells you whether "doesn't wait" survives a slow disk.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body:
The websocket fan-out problem is the real one — cleanly distributing a single tick stream to chart rendering, script re-evaluation, watchlist updates, and live order state without one component blocking or lagging the others is genuinely hard to get right, and that's usually the wall that ends most "let's build our own trading terminal" projects, so it's a credible thing to point to as a year well spent.

A few honest questions rather than just congratulations: the <1ms tick-to-order claim — is that measured at the order engine boundary (received tick to order object constructed) or all the way through broker API round-trip? Those are very different numbers and worth being precise about publicly, since the second one is largely out of your control once it leaves your system. Also curious how the RMS behaves under a burst — if 50 positions all breach a risk rule in the same tick because of a market-wide gap, does the engine process them sequentially or is there real concurrency handling there, since that's usually where "advanced RMS" claims get tested for real.

The unified data/order API across brokers and asset classes is the part I'd actually want to poke at hardest, since normalizing options chains, futures, and equities under one clean abstraction without leaky edge cases is its own multi-year problem on top of the fan-out one — that's the same plumbing challenge EventTrader's had to solve on the data-normalization side, so I get exactly how much is being underclaimed in that one line of your post.
